summary: Streaming disconnects during first production test (SSE) — customer unsure if server issue vs expected client behavior
description:
Customer (Bluepeak AI) is running their first production-like test against Hosted API streaming responses and seeing intermittent disconnects. They are unsure whether this indicates a Redwood outage/instability or expected behavior of SSE over the public internet and want recommended production-safe client patterns (timeouts/retries/reconnect) before go-live.

Issue summary
- Streaming chat occasionally terminates mid-generation; client reports network error; no final "[DONE]" marker observed.
- Frequency: ~1–3% of requests during a 20–30 minute test (reported), higher when run behind their corporate proxy / k8s ingress.
- Customer confusion: expects "streaming" to be reliable and complete; does not have reconnect logic or clear understanding of which errors are retriable.

Impact
- Blocks planned limited production rollout; customer concerned they will show partial responses to end-users.
- Support load: repeats a top onboarding theme (streaming disconnect confusion) that we intend to mitigate via the in-console onboarding checklist + SDK defaults.

Environment
- Hosted API, prod, us-east.
- Customer stack: Node.js 20 + TypeScript SDK (reported). Running from a Kubernetes cluster behind an ingress controller (nginx) and (sometimes) corporate egress proxy.
- Streaming mode: SSE (event stream). They are using a server-to-server call (not browser).

Steps to reproduce (from customer)
1) Create a simple endpoint that forwards prompts to Redwood streaming chat and relays tokens to client.
2) Run a load test (20 concurrent users, 60s average response, mix of short and long prompts).
3) Observe some streams end early with a network error; response to end-user is truncated.

Customer-provided symptoms / excerpts
- Node client error: "TypeError: fetch failed" / "UND_ERR_SOCKET" (undici) / "ECONNRESET".
- In a few runs, they observed HTTP 499 on their ingress logs (client closed request).
- They were not sure which timeouts apply (client vs server vs proxy) and asked if there is a Redwood recommended read timeout.

Redwood-side initial checks (support)
- No corresponding elevated 5xx rate in us-east for their tenant in the same timeframe.
- No sustained gateway saturation observed; some individual requests show normal completion times.
- Hypothesis: client/proxy timeout/idle timeout or downstream disconnect, plus lack of reconnect/backoff logic on the customer side.

What the customer asked for
- Confirmation whether Redwood streaming can disconnect mid-stream without an error from Redwood.
- A recommended approach to: (a) detect partial completion, (b) retry safely, (c) reconnect/resume if possible.
- Guidance they can use in their internal production readiness checklist.

Attachments
- Customer included request IDs for 6 failures in email; copied into internal notes in comments below (not pasted here to avoid leaking identifiers outside the ticket).
comments: 2025-03-04 (Priya Shah, Support): Acknowledged. Asked customer for: (1) exact SDK version, (2) whether calls originate from browser vs backend, (3) ingress/proxy timeouts (nginx proxy_read_timeout, idle timeout), (4) 3–5 request IDs + timestamps (UTC) for failed streams, (5) whether they see 499/504 on their side. Also asked them to confirm they are consuming the stream continuously (not buffering).

2025-03-04 (Customer, Bluepeak AI via Support): Using Node 20, TS SDK "~0.18.x" (they weren’t sure exact patch). Calls are backend-to-backend. They run behind nginx ingress; proxy_read_timeout currently 60s, idle timeout default. They see some 499s and occasional 504s on nginx when it happens; app logs show ECONNRESET. Provided 6 request IDs + timestamps between 17:10–17:42 UTC.

2025-03-05 (Sean Gallagher, SRE): Checked service health for us-east during provided window: no incident, no elevated 5xx or disconnect anomalies at fleet level. For the provided request IDs that completed on our side, logs indicate normal token emission; a subset show downstream disconnect mid-stream (client closed) rather than server termination. Suggest focusing on proxy/client keepalive + read timeouts + retry guidance.

2025-03-05 (Ibrahim Khan, SDK): In Node/undici, streaming can surface as ECONNRESET/UND_ERR_SOCKET when the upstream (proxy/ingress) closes idle connections or when backpressure stalls reads. We should recommend: (a) set explicit timeouts on client and proxy to exceed worst-case generation time, (b) implement retry w/ backoff for retryable network errors before first token, (c) for mid-stream disconnect, decide UX (show partial + "regenerating"), then retry from scratch with idempotency key so server can dedupe if applicable. Note: true resume from mid-stream isn’t supported today; we can only restart the request.

2025-03-06 (Priya Shah, Support): Shared with customer: Redwood does not guarantee SSE streams will never disconnect across the internet; clients must handle disconnects. Recommended increasing nginx proxy_read_timeout to 300s+ for long outputs and confirming upstream keepalive settings. Also recommended adding a 'stream established' watchdog (if no token within N seconds, abort + retry). Asked them to test directly (no corporate proxy) to isolate.

2025-03-07 (Customer, Bluepeak AI via Support): Testing directly from a VM (no corporate proxy) reduced failures significantly (near zero in 30 min). Behind proxy + ingress still seeing ~1% truncated responses. They can raise proxy_read_timeout to 300s. They asked for official Redwood docs they can cite internally.

2025-03-07 (Wei Chen, Docs): We have a gap: streaming troubleshooting + reconnect patterns are scattered. This ticket matches what #docs flagged. We can add a short section under the new onboarding checklist docs: 'Streaming: handle disconnects (reconnect + retries + proxy timeouts)'.

2025-03-10 (Ibrahim Khan, SDK): Pointed Support to upcoming improvements: examples repo has a prod-ready streaming example w/ retry/backoff + structured logging; Go SDK has reconnect helper; Python SDK has retry/timeout presets. TS SDK docs/snippets are being updated to include safer streaming usage and recommended timeouts. Linked PRs in ticket fields.

2025-03-11 (Priya Shah, Support): Follow-up to customer: Provided concrete recommendations (below) and asked them to re-run test after increasing nginx/proxy timeouts and adding retry logic. Offered to review their nginx settings if they paste sanitized config blocks.

2025-03-12 (Priya Shah, Support): Customer confirmed improved stability after setting proxy_read_timeout=300s and disabling an aggressive egress proxy idle timeout for the test namespace. They are implementing retry logic before go-live. Marking resolved; keeping linked follow-ups for docs/checklist/SDK guidance.
resolution:
Not a Redwood platform incident. Root cause was primarily downstream disconnects introduced by customer networking (ingress/proxy idle/read timeouts) plus missing client-side resiliency patterns for SSE streaming. Redwood-side logs indicated client-initiated disconnects in failure cases (downstream closed) and no correlated us-east service degradation.

Workaround / guidance provided to customer
- Increase proxy/ingress timeouts for streaming routes (e.g., nginx proxy_read_timeout and upstream idle timeouts) to exceed worst-case generation time (recommended starting point: 300s for initial prod tests).
- Ensure HTTP keep-alives are enabled end-to-end; avoid buffering the stream.
- Implement retry/backoff for retryable network errors (especially before first token). For mid-stream disconnects, restart request from scratch and present appropriate UX (partial output + regeneration). Resume-from-mid-stream is not supported today.
- Add request correlation (request ID, tenant, timestamp) to logs to simplify future investigations.

Product/docs follow-ups (tracked outside Jira)
- Add explicit onboarding checklist step guidance for 'Streaming: handle disconnects' with recommended timeout/retry defaults and proxy gotchas.
- Align SDK examples/snippets with production-safe streaming patterns.

Customer outcome
- After raising proxy_read_timeout and adjusting proxy behavior, customer reports disconnect rate near zero in re-test; proceeding with a limited rollout.
internal_notes: Support macro update requested: include a standard set of questions for streaming issues (browser vs backend, proxy/ingress timeouts, 499/504 presence, SDK version, whether first token is received, and whether disconnect correlates with long outputs). This maps directly to the Guided Onboarding / First Production Launch checklist content. Reference: Confluence production-readiness SDK recommendations + checklist template.
external_customer_update: We reviewed your request IDs and did not find evidence of a Redwood-side outage or elevated error rates. The disconnects match downstream connection closes (often ingress/proxy timeout/idle settings). Streaming over SSE requires client-side resiliency: set longer proxy read/idle timeouts for streaming endpoints, ensure keep-alives, and implement retry/backoff for transient network errors. For mid-stream disconnects, the recommended approach today is to restart the request (resume isn’t currently supported). We can share updated docs/examples as they land, and we’re also adding clearer guidance to our 'first production launch' checklist.
